utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-02-60-T, the Prosecutor versus Vidoje Blagojevic and Dragan Jokic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ladies and gentlemen, good morning. We'll continue the proceeding today. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. McCloskey [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stupar. Yesterday you had mentioned a report that you had I believe signed off on. We'll get to that in a minute. But prior to you coming to The Hague, you understood that this issue of you -- whether or not you were in command on these days was going to be an issue in your testimony, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure the interpreters heard you. I think like yesterday we need to remember speak up if you can. So you did know that this was going to be an issue?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you make any effort to go through your records, any personnel file, any of the older MUP records to try to find, you know, your annual leave records or your leave slips or anything like that that might help this issue?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have my annual leave records. I never received them. As for our pay slips, annual leave was not recorded in these and I'm not sure we were even receiving our pay at that time. The only thing I tried to find was my request to be relieved of my duty on the 19th of May, 1995, as commander of the detachment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you able to find any -- were you able to find that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ask the MUP for your annual leave records?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received any document, nor were documents issued at that time for annual leave or anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I know you said that, but did you ask the -- your employers to look for any possible records that they would have kept after you had informed them of the annual leave?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you can still do that, can't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The problem, however, is that the brigade as such was disbanded and I have no idea where the archives are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I know finding records from the war can be difficult, but if you do make an effort and if you do find anything, we would certainly appreciate getting those documents that could benefit you in the long run. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think -- I take that a veiled threat to the witness, as if somehow he's on trial at this point in time. I want the record to reflect that the gentleman informed the Office of the Prosecution back in 2002 that he was on annual leave. Then it becomes incumbent upon the Prosecution, since he was interviewed as a suspect to go look at his records.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to these dialogues, and it's inflaming the witness. That was anything but a threat, asking him to help us out by getting his annual leave records, for God's sake.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you understand that if you were --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: You understand --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we have a slight technical problem now. Do you understand that if you are able to find any records that'll shed some light on this, we would gladly accept them?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And I have a few records that we can go over and you can help explain those and how they may fit in to what you've been telling us. So let's first start with what has been marked as P853. If we could give the witness a B/C/S version of that and give him a moment to take a look at it. You had mentioned yesterday this report when I was asking you and -- or something that sounded like this report. If you could just take a minute to look at it and let us know if you think this is what you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could put the last page of the B/C/S on the ELMO. We've got an original that might be -- the witness can take a look at that as well. Can you put it so we can see the signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that appear to be the document you mentioned to us yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is one of the documents that was mentioned yesterday, the report for the first six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And did you sign that document? Is that your signature in that inked original that you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you did sign it as commander of the 2nd Detachment in Sekovici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I signed it on the 15th of July, 1995, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And we note that on the front of that document it's dated 5 July, but on the right-hand corner it's handwritten 15 July. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. 15th July, that's when it was signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's when, as you told us yesterday, you came in to the office before going to Zvornik and you did some paperwork?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not paperwork. As I said, this was supposed to have been already sent and I had been in charge for most of this. And I had provided monthly reports for the work of the detachment, and this was a six-month report. The late Oficir wasn't there; he had gone to Kula and this had to be sent off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was some period of time in this report that you signed for, but you weren't involved in as commander, I take it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the last 15 days of June, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've told us you stopped being commander on 15 June, and this report went through 30 June. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I think that in June it should say that the detachment was still in Sarajevo so that there was actually no report for June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you will look under the heading "Engagement in police work in the first half of 1995" - do you find that section? - you can see there on the second paragraph there talks about: "Between 1 January 1995 and 30 June 1995, 6 policemen were daily engaged in guarding facilities and material and technical equipment in Tisca where the depots are and in Sekovici where the detachment headquarters is."

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It also talks about policemen being involved in the forward communication centre and Backovic and Sekovici. So it does involve some time period into June 30th, up to June 30th. If you could also take a look farther down there under "The state of readiness in the unit headquarters" section. I asked you yesterday if you remember whether or not there was a tank crew or -- a Praga crew ever in readiness in Bratunac. If you could take a look at that, perhaps that will refresh your recollection. As you can see under the state of readiness it says that: "Between 18 March and 30 June 1995, a tank crew was in a state of readiness in Bratunac. Four policemen, 105 days."

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Just a moment. Please. It says: "From the 1st of March to the 31st of March Praga crew on standby," and so on. "Four members" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps you've got the wrong -- I think there's another version of this report. Well, let's -- do you see between 18 March 1995 and 30 June 1995? It's the -- it should be around the third line down under "State of Readiness."

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do see it. But here you see from the 1st of April to the 30th of April, the Praga crew was on standby in Sekovici. There is a paragraph here. You see from the 18th of March, 1995, to the 30th of June, 1995, the tank crew was on standby in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. That's what I'm referring to. Does that help your recollection? Was there a tank crew standing by in Bratunac on those dates, March through 30 June 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible there was; I don't remember. I can't remember it, but it's possible, yes. What is confusing here that it says: "From the 1st to the 30th of April, the Praga crew and the tank crew on standby in headquarters."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So do you recall sending the tank crew to Bratunac in 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible it was sent there. I don't remember exactly, but it's possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the tank would have been sent with the crew I take it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you read in Mr. -- in this report that may have been written by Mr. Borovcanin, he talks about a Praga and a BOV being assigned along the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road. And he mentions both the -- your unit and the 1st Company PJP Zvornik. Do you remember reading that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, having looked at this document and thought about that report that Mr. Borovcanin has written, the Praga and the BOV along that road, do you know whose they were?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see them, so I don't know whose they were. But as of 2002 when I made my statement in Banja Luka, on my return from Banja Luka, I talked to some members of the detachment. And they said to me that the technical equipment of the 2nd Detachment was engaged in Bratunac at the time Srebrenica fell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was engaged in Bratunac or Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It -- during the work in Srebrenica, they were engaged in Bratunac. That's what they told me; however, I didn't know this when I was making my statement in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So today now you're telling us that you found information that the Praga and the BOV were in Bratunac during the Srebrenica dates?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were shown pictures and video of the Praga and the BOV along the road originally to the Office of the Prosecutor, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you at that time said you didn't recognise those vehicles. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't recognise them, because all these vehicles looked the same. They're all mass produced, and they all look the same.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't recognise your own vehicles because they looked the same?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these vehicles look alike. And I did say that there were no distinguishing features that would help me to recognise them. I only know that our vehicles had blue licence plates, but on those pictures I couldn't see any licence plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Going near the end of the report, there's a section that talks about -- that is entitled: "Cooperation with SJB, VRS commands, and institutions and governments organs." "Cooperation with SJB," what is just the SJB? We've heard a lot of initials.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public security station, that's the present-day police station in Sekovici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Then it says: "VRS commands." And down in the second paragraph, you talk about the cooperation with the command of the 1st VRS Birac Brigade in Sekovici. And you say it's poor, but then you say: "Well, the cooperation with the battalion commands in the territory of the municipality is good. And battalion commanders inform us all about all intelligence-related events." So you're saying you got along with the battalion commanders, but the commander himself there wasn't a very good relationship with?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would that have been -- I believe he was a colonel or perhaps a Lieutenant Colonel Svetozar Andric at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How important is your coordination and relationships with the VRS units that you're working with?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's important if I'm working with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us why it's important, what aspects of it. Give us a little more detail about that so we can try to understand. For example, this is a wartime situation. We can read your report. We can see that you're working with -- we know you're working with the army. People -- your guys are getting killed. So in the context of a war when you're working together with the army, where people are being killed, how important is your relationship and good communication with those that you're working with? Can you give us a feel for that.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the communication is important; it's essential.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would have been essential for the 2nd Sekovici Detachment to be communicating with its army cooperators in any battlefield, is that correct, that they're working with the army on?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The chief differences with the commander of the Birac Brigade was on raising the units up to manpower level. When we had to do that, have someone transferred to our unit, we had to have approval from the army and the Ministry of Defence. But he did not allow this to happen, and that was the main reason why we were, so to say, not on the best of terms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in the combat operations you were with with the army, they shared intelligence with you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't real intelligent information in the sense you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know what I mean? I'm just talking about basic military intelligence, combat intelligence, where the enemy is, what prisoners are saying.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we were in the area, they probably knew us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say here --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Told us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah. So it only makes sense that if you're working with the army, they will give you their intelligence, like you say here in this report?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no intelligence information, really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're looking at this Court today and telling them you had no intelligence information in combat activities in this war? Is that what you're saying? No intelligence, really?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Poor intelligence. There was very little of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, here you say that the battalion commanders informed you about all the intelligence-related events. You're aware that the VRS had excellent capabilities for intercepting enemy communications, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour, I want to object at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have had no testimony with respect to the VRS. We have had lots of testimony with respect to the Muslim intelligence capabilities of intercepting, but I -- we have yet to hear any concrete evidence and anything -- nothing has been presented with respect to VRS capabilities. So making this statement is a fact not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I think this is in the cross-examination, they could present a case to us with this witness and this witness could answer according to his knowledge. I don't think there's any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are treating both parties on equal footing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour, but when counsel makes a representation, there has to be a fact as to that representation, unless he's going to present us with some evidence. What I'm suggesting is to say the VRS had excellent communication, we haven't heard any testimony, so now counsel is testifying. So that's what I'm saying at this point. If he wants to lay a foundation or tell us how he came up with that conclusion, maybe there's no objection, but the way it's stated based on the evidence as I understand it that has come into this case, there's nothing for him to say that. He can assume because the Muslim authorities had these capabilities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey, you may break up your question, going step by step. First ask about the VRS's intelligence ability.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I know it's been a long case, but we have intelligence reports by the VRS that cite that they're getting radio intercept messages. It's in evidence, it was discussed by Butler, it's all over the place. Mr. Obrenovic -- He's maybe a mistake like he did in his allegation against me yesterday. But there's plenty of foundation for that in this case, and the witness should know that there is as well. So if I would just respond to Mr. Karnavas's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, that solves it then. You don't remember. I won't ask you about it, then. Let's go to the Zvornik Brigade. You have told us that when you were together with Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Borovcanin and Mr. Vasic and I think another person at the Zvornik Brigade, there was discussion of this very difficult situation and that most of the -- that you felt it would be best to open up an area, let the Muslim column through. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when Pandurevic arrived, he told you and the whole group that he had orders and that there would be a double line to stop those remaining Muslims coming through. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later, as you've told us, the -- there was a decision made to, in fact -- after a horrible battle, to in fact allow those Muslims through. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. They made the decision. I had nothing to -- when we went out of the siege, they said the decision had been made to let them leave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that was a VRS decision?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Pandurevic was up there. Probably, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that Pandurevic a few days later got in big trouble for that decision and that members of the Main Staff came up to look into that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that time you were in the Zvornik -- at the headquarters there with this group, was the Kravica incident brought up and discussed, or mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, at that time on the 15th of July, were you aware that hundreds and hundreds of Muslims had been murdered at the Kravica warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never heard about it, despite the fact that you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it sometime in 1998, 1999, around about that time -- maybe 1996, 1997, but anyway a long time later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the first time you heard about the Kravica warehouse massacre was sometime in 1996?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly, but later. I heard about it later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Obrenovic testified that that was a matter that was discussed openly amongst all of you, the massacre at Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Obrenovic lied. He wasn't telling the truth when he said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you think of Mr. Obrenovic pleading guilty and acknowledging he --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're not trying Mr. Obrenovic and I think this is an improper question. What the gentleman thinks about Mr. Obrenovic doing, whether he pled guilty or not guilty has nothing to do with it, because then what if those who chose to exercise their right to go to trial, does that mean somehow that they're guilty because they're going to trial, versus those who have pled out like Momir Nikolic, the fountain of truth. I think it's unfair to pose this question to the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. McCloskey has not finished his question. You don't know what his question is. Let us hear the question first.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can go on, though the interpretation of what that question was supposed to mean is certainly nothing related to the reason for the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to show you that -- some of these video clips again briefly. And this is from our -- an exhibit that was marked P21 -- I'm sorry, before I do that, there's another document I want to ask you about. So I might as well finish up the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P850. It's not dated as far as I can see, and it's entitled: "Personnel questionnaire." And if you can just take a look at that and I'll ask you about some of the notations on it. Do you know what this document is? Is it something you recall filling out or do you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a personal questionnaire to establish rank of an authorised official. I don't know when that -- what year that was, but I don't remember ever having filled out this form.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's just go over a couple of things in it. Let's look at that number 6, the service record, where it says: "Deputy commander from 8 March 1993 to 10 June 1993." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says: "Company commander from 11 June 1993 to 19 February 1993." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it says: "2nd Sekovici Detachment commander from 20 February 1994 to 22 August 1995." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct according to the record and authorisation, but when I was talking a moment ago, the administration was always late. So this was a certificate once I was relieved of duty and the commander's list was the 28th. So pursuant to the authorisation. And in actual fact, on the 15th of June, 1995, was when I handed over the detachment and I commanded until the 15th and until some officers had come back from sick leave. That was about ten days, and then the other person continued.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you testified in direct that you were a commander on paper. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's very difficult for me to explain this to you. You come from a country where everything is well-ordered, so it's very difficult to explain the situation of a country that was at war with respect to paperwork and administrations. I really don't know what to tell you. I'm saying judging by the paper, the authorisation, I was commander from the 22nd of August. I said what the situation was like and what the command was like actually on the ground. So do I have to explain to you that it was at a time when the ministers had great powers, and he could relieve and appoint commanders from one day to the next without any paperwork, any authorisation on paper. Do you think that everything was done on the basis of paper at that time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're just repeating what you said in direct, that you were a commander on paper. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it says here. All that is written down here, on the 22nd of August 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And we won't get into how well-organised my country is in this time of warfare either. Let's look down at 7.4. It says: "As OSL or in VRS from 1 April 1992 to 20 April 1995." Do you know what that is a reference to? Did -- and where the date 20 April 1995 came from?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it says: "In special combat police brigade from 1 April 1992 to 20 April 1995." Could that be a reference to you going on leave on 20 April 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you went on leave 15 June 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there's some other documents, but they're basically similar and I don't feel the need to go over them. Let's show the video.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm told that it's not working. Okay. I guess we need to start it again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that working, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. That's --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take it we're going to have some foundation as to what location that was. Are they going to be asking this gentleman some questions, given that we know where he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He has said he hasn't seen any of these things, so I'm just asking him about these machines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It all depends on where this is happening. That's what I'm saying. We have to establish, if you can lay a foundation, where this occurred, because we're talking a large territory. So it's possible to be someplace and not see this because this is happening someplace else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We just saw the clips of the video footage. The question has not been asked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll come back and try to get a freeze shot, but is it fair to say that one of those machines was a Praga and one of them was a BOV?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us, now that we have this freeze frame, which is which here? The one closest to us in front of the screen, which is that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a BOV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And -- so the other one is a Praga. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these are designed as anti-aircraft weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you've said, you weren't -- you didn't see any of this equipment along the Bratunac/Konjevic Polje road while you were there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I was only there up to Sandici. Just up to Sandici was where I was. So Bratunac/Sandici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is very close to the area of Sandici on the afternoon of 13 July.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now we have the Prosecutor testifying where this was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I thought that's what you wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would like to know how he's making this statement that this is near Sandici. Because between Sandici and Konjevic Polje, it's quite a long distance. So if he could lay a foundation. Who said that this was by Sandici? It's a long stretch of road; that's what I'm saying. So he needs to establish through a witness, through prior testimony, that so-and-so said that this occurred in such-and-such a place. If that's the case, then it's a fair question. But for him to make that representation, counsel now is testifying, and that's what I object to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I see no problem in this aspect, Mr. Karnavas. And the witness answered that question already.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the problem is: We have the lawyer testifying, giving evidence. It's like me giving evidence as if I'm a witness. If there was a foundation that somebody else has said: "This occurred at this location," then I think it's -- then we know at least there's testimony, whether it's right or wrong, that -- but there's testimony that somebody said this happened at this location, where the gentleman might have been. But because it's a long stretch of road, and that's what I'm saying. I don't remember any evidence coming in through a particular witness saying this incident here occurred at this location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- but anyway, Mr. McCloskey, can you tell us what's the foundation for that location?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we have to go back a long time ago to Mr. Ruez I think who -- I think this original, as you remember, that Potocari, the other film, Mr. Ruez talked about it to give you a background on it and what we knew about it. And it's my understanding as long as I have a good-faith belief in the truth and foundation of my question and that it's something I can back up, I can ask a question based on it. The points that Mr. Karnavas are making is a point that I'm not even contesting. This man has said he didn't see this there; that's over. We're on another subject.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as you looked at this video today and as you after, I think, speaking to the OTP have heard that your equipment was in Bratunac at the Srebrenica time and you take a good look at this, does this look like your equipment to you, very distinctive blue splotch on the back of that front one. And there's some white paint marks -- some sort of white marks on the back of the other one? Was this help you at all?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say one thing: This isn't my equipment, it is the equipment of the 2nd Detachment of Sekovici. And last time I told you that I was able to identify that it was the 2nd Detachment, or rather, had it been there I would have said. But I'm saying again that our vehicles had blue licence plates, and every vehicle was registered. I don't see any licence plates here at all. So maybe they do belong to the 2nd Detachment or maybe they don't, because they were mass produced, these vehicles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to another section of the video, which is in the area of Sandici. We should all be able to recognise it. I know there's been testimony specifically on that. And you have already testified that you were in the area of Sandici and that you saw Mr. Trifunovic there. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to remind us all, Mr. Trifunovic was one of the platoon commanders of the 2nd Sekovici Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he was. He was the commanding officer of the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person there in the headband?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's Cop, and I recognised him last time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's the one that's speaking to this man that is calling out for his son to come out of the woods?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he's saying it to that man. I don't know what he's doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's continue with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Trifunovic, commander of the platoon, is telling this Muslim man to call people down from the woods, isn't he? Would that be your take on that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would Trifunovic have done that on his own or would he have received orders to take part in the process to bring Muslims down from the woods?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think a platoon commander might do something of that significance all by himself without any commander telling him to do it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were in Sandici for how many hours?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two, I think, perhaps three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said two or three hours. Did you see any of this?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to all those men in the field that we saw in the video?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any idea?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you believe the allegations that they were all murdered?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any dead bodies while you were in Sandici? I won't show you the video that shows that, the bodies.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is the case of the Prosecution that at that time there was an organised process to capture and detain and separate adult male men for execution. And as part of that process, young men after the age of -- born after -- approximately 1980 were taken out of the Sandici meadow and allowed to go free, and that process happened during a good part of the day in Sandici. You were there for two, three hours. Did you witness the process by which young men were called out by the Serb soldiers? "Anyone that has been born after 1980 may stand up." Did you observe that, that process, happening?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some young men stood up and were allowed to go. Some young men stood up and were told to sit down. You saw none of that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did see army present in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Sekovici detachment have anything to do with the organised transportation in buses and trucks of Muslim prisoners from Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have any trucks and buses at your disposal at that time to be able to use?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either -- actually, I'm not quite clear on your question. Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the 2nd Sekovici Detachment have the ability to access large numbers of buses and trucks for the transportation of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've said that you -- that Oficir or Mr. Cuturic who later died in combat in another theatre of operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have said that he went with a soldier named Krsto up towards the Kravica warehouse that afternoon and some -- shortly thereafter you heard quite a bit of gunfire. Can you describe that gunfire for us, how long was it, what kind of gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all I can say is that it was intensive, so not sporadic fire, but intensive fire. Although I can't tell you for how long. I don't remember exactly when.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you distinguish whether or not it was your typical 7.62 Kalashnikov automatic weapon that most soldiers carry versus say 50 calibre machine-gun? Could you make out the calibre, the size of the shooting?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From what you heard, could you distinguish the kind of weapons that you thought doing the firing? I've heard soldiers get good at that after a while.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, as far as I can recall, there were infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, did the infantry carry the 7.62 automatic AK 47 Kalashnikov? Is that what you mean when you say infantry weapons?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were carrying Kalashnikovs. There were also light machine-guns and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And how long -- sorry. Did you hear any other -- any explosions, detonations, like hand grenades or larger-calibre explosions like RPGs, rocket-propelled grenades?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at that point in time, no. Not then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When I left, I didn't hear that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And about how long did this intense firing go on for?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact time now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't -- nobody can remember exact times, but can you just give us a feeling for it. Was it more than a minute? More than five minutes?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, surely you know how long it takes to take a full clip from a Kalashnikov and fire it on automatic until it's empty. How long does that take?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No idea?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not that I have no idea, but I never calculated that and it's been nine years since I've been firing those kinds of weapons. It's fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Less than a minute?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think about a minute, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after emptying a full clip, is the barrel hot enough to burn yourself if you grab it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I never tried it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the more you fire your Kalashnikov, the hotter the barrel is going to get?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you have told us you had access to a Motorola while you were there in Sandici. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Motorola that I took from Cop at that moment when the shooting was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if an army officer had a Motorola and was within range, he could speak to you on your Motorola, couldn't he, if he was on the right channel?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was on the same channel, yes, he could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your call sign at that time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: For whom?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For you. You had a call sign, didn't you? I mean --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I had a call sign at that point, but usually I was Laser 61.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you remember what Borovcanin's call sign was at that time period?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Laser 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Laser 1, if anyone?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Laser 1 was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Saric, Goran Saric, the commander of the special brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Laser 3?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Milutin Erakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Laser 4?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the man for the rear, but I can't remember his name now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you get this call, you heard Krsto is dead. You've just heard intense firing. You've heard Krsto is dead and that one of the commanders, Mr. Cuturic or Oficir is wounded. So this is a pretty serious situation and you get in your car and go there immediately. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I called Oficir. I asked him what was going on there. He said that Krsto was dead and that he was wounded. At that point, I called Ljubisa. I don't actually remember whether I called him or whether he called me, because it's possible he may have heard me but not Oficir and that he asked me what was going on up there. And I said things were not well with Oficir. And then I left that Motorola and I set out immediately over there because he had asked me to come and take him to the doctor's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so you go to the area of the warehouse and you saw him standing on the road in front of the -- some 10 to 15 metres from the warehouse is what you said. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 10 or 20 metres, something like that. But he was standing on the road. I think there's even a gate there leading to the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said you saw some soldiers firing weapons. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw some soldiers and I heard sporadic gunfire, but I didn't see them actually firing. I just saw them standing around there. I can't say that I saw them holding a rifle and firing, but you could hear sporadic gunfire of less intensity than I described previously. It was sporadic, not intense now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the soldiers were standing around where?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around that warehouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any buses in front of the warehouse then?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any at that point. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were looking over at the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I wanted to open the door for the late Oficir to get him into the car and drive on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you knew there were -- so you were looking at the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was looking toward the late Oficir so that I could open the door for him. I leaned over to open the door and I could see a little behind him, but I was focusing on him. And I opened the door and he got in and we drove on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were looking over towards the warehouse where you saw the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I wasn't paying that much attention to them. I just saw them standing there and I heard the gunfire. That's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you knew there was Muslim prisoners being held there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that at that point in time, no, until the late Oficir started telling me what had happened to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've already testified that Krsto came up to Oficir and said that he heard one of his Muslim neighbours might be up there and he wanted to go see him. So given that, you should have known that there was Muslims up there. And I believe you've testified you've seen or you've said before you've seen Muslims being walked in that direction by unknown army soldiers. So let's think about that answer. You knew there were Muslims up there, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know there were Muslims there. I did say they were taken that direction. I did say that Oficir went in that direction with Krle, but I didn't know where they were. When I set out, I didn't even know where I would find the late Oficir, I didn't know that. If he hadn't been standing on the road, I wouldn't have known where to look for him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked over towards the warehouse, did you see Muslim bodies?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had heard long periods of automatic gunfire and you looked right over at that warehouse where the soldiers were.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't look into the warehouse. I just leaned over to open the door for the late Oficir. That's how much I could see. It lasted about a second. It was just a glance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Cuturic, Oficir, had burned his hand -- his hands, and you had to rush him to the hospital and leave the Kravica warehouse without noticing anything at the Kravica warehouse. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. As soon as he got in, he said: "Drive on quickly. I'm in pain." I set out, started driving, and then I said: "What happened?" And then as we were driving along, he continued his story.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to his story, a Muslim jumped out, took a gun, and started shooting. And he grabbed the barrel and stopped it. That's the basic story, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, I mean if he's going to be paraphrasing, he should be paraphrasing correctly. Stop what? I would just like to be -- I want the Prosecutor to be fair. He can cross-examine vigorously, continuously, and lengthy, but he's got to be fair. If he's going to paraphrase, he should paraphrase correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: This is the basic story, the Prosecution said, basic. If there's anything wrong, I believe that the witness could correct that point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me tell you one thing: You may have misunderstood or maybe you're misquoting. The Muslims didn't come outside and take his rifle. He went in to look for someone, so he stepped in. He took a step or two inside. That's what he said, at least, and they grabbed him and then they grabbed his rifle away from him and fired a few shots. And they killed Krsto there. At that moment, he went in to pull Krsto out. And as they already had the rifle in their hands, they pointed it at Oficir and he grabbed it by the barrel. He hadn't gone far in; he was by the door. And they shot it until they fired all the bullets. Then he started running back. At least, that's his story, what he told me. And that was the injury he sustained, that was a burn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's the story he told you. Now --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also plausible -- let's -- given we have the medical record that shows Cuturic has burns on his palms, we have the medical record that shows Krsto was killed at about that time, at about that place, we have another medical record showing somebody else was wounded at about that time, at about that place; and we have the story that you've been told. Did you ever hear this version of events, that officers, soldiers, MUP, people in camouflage uniforms stood around the opening of the warehouse with their automatic weapons and suddenly opened fire on a crowd of some 400 to 500 Muslims at one end of the warehouse, while at the other end of the warehouse the soldiers are telling the Muslims: "Look what your people are doing, they're attacking us." And that while the soldiers or MUP, the people in camouflage, are firing into this crowd of 400 or 500 Muslims, a Muslim crazily breaks out, grabs a weapon, kills Krsto, wounds somebody else. Cuturic grabs the weapon. And that's how he burned his hands. Have you heard that side of the story?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to that. It's not even a question. It's mischaracterised the facts. If he wishes to say: We have this witness who said that and this witness who said that and then to give the opportunity to the gentleman to see whether he heard those stories, I don't have a problem. But this paraphrasing that on the other end they're saying: "Look what these people are doing." And then somebody else saying -- this whole incident. It's a total mischaracterisation, and there is no relevance to it. If he wants to ask a question like that, then at least he should be straight with the facts. Tell the gentleman who said what at that point in time and be correct with the facts. The summary of the events, as presented by Mr. McCloskey, are rather embellished.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If I may respond to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, and I can find the -- he has read the very witness statement out to this Court where the Kravica survivor at the other end of the warehouse is relating to what the guard is talking to him while he's hearing shooting. Mr. Karnavas read that out, and that's also part of this record, as is the testimony of both Kravica warehouse survivors who say that this shooting suddenly started from nowhere. So the hypothetical or the interpretation of the question is based firmly on fact. This witness is giving us a hearsay account of this thing. He's not an eyewitness to it. So as he has said himself, this is the story he's heard. I've asked him if he's heard the other story which fundamentally may be the truth. The fact is this may be a mystery that lives well beyond all of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've got two survivors. I really have absolutely no objection to Mr. McCloskey reading the relevant portions from the survivors' statements and say: "Witness one says this, witness two says that. Now you're telling us this." I don't have a problem with that. I do have a problem with the way the facts are sort of put together in this hypothetical or his -- it's not a hypothetical in his belief of what the testimony has been. That's what I'm saying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, you know that this witness is not an eyewitness to that particular witness. Whatever he told us is hearsay evidence. I believe the Prosecution could put his case before this witness. The only question the witness needs to answer is a yes or no answer. Whatever he answers has very little relevance to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. I just -- from a technical standpoint, as a technician in court --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm objecting. The constant backtalking in front of the witness is just completely inappropriate and is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it's time for a break, Mr. McCloskey. Would you please finish this question and maybe we'll have a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have one or two questions and a very short video and I'm through. So if we could go for a couple more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Though we may have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Of course, there's other people in the room. This shouldn't take long.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you hear the story, the version, that I had --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you didn't discuss either -- any version of the Kravica events with Mr. Obrenovic on 15 July?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I want to show you a video segment that we believe was shot on the afternoon of the 13th of July as someone was driving by the warehouse. And it will be slow motion so that you can get a better look at it, and I want to ask you a few questions about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now here's the slow motion of that last segment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise what the pile of objects were in front of the warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They looked like dead people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you looked over at the warehouse that afternoon, did you see anything that looked like that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did 2nd Sekovici soldiers wear one-piece jumpsuits that day in Sandici?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they did, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sometimes when it gets hot, in order to get out of the top of the jumpsuit, you take it off and roll it down and tie it around your waist?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But other soldiers had such jumpsuits, too. It wasn't just the Sekovici detachment wearing jumpsuits.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, do you have any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think a break would be in order at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, if you insist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't insist, Your Honour. I'm just saying that I'm going to go on for -- well, not some time but a little bit of time. We could all use the break, especially the people in the booth and the interpreters, so I'm looking after their welfare as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll resume at 10 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, your re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas, I believe that you should re-arrange your gown, otherwise your image on television may not be so presentable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. President, Your Honours. My apologies. And thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stupar.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You're going to have to speak up a little bit louder. I just want to go through some of the documents, some that were shown and some that were not shown. So first if I could show you Exhibit P850 for identification. That was -- this won't take long. Now, obviously this is a personnel questionnaire. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what your date of birth is on this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: 7th December 1963.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And is that the correct date?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, this is the document that was referred to by the Prosecutor under column 6, was it not, that designated you as the deputy company commander or the commander of the 2nd Detachment -- 2nd Sekovici Detachment from 20 February 1994 to August 22nd, 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we understand your testimony correctly, you're disputing those dates?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, following that it says that you were the chief of the Zvornik section of anti-terrorist administration. And it states from 23 August 1995 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, was that a position you took up after leaving the 2nd Detachment, 2nd Sekovici Detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is that date correct, 23rd August 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What about in your own mind, given that you now have disputed some of the dates?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that on the 15th of June I orally agreed with the minister Tomo Kovac that I should be transferred to this anti-terrorist administration to the Zvornik department, and that Oficir should take command of the detachment. However, this document was late and I only received it later on because the administration wasn't working properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, do you remember about what date you started working as the chief of the anti-terrorist administration in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This administration was supposed to be set up, but it never actually came alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let me rephrase the question. In your mind, when did you take up this position or did you ever take it up in light of your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: De facto this administration never existed. There were attempts to set it up. I was there, I think, for a year. I had this document appointing me to that position, but I didn't actually do any work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to show you what has been marked as P851 for identification, and I just have one quick question for you. Now, that is -- this is your workbook, is it not, or a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, this is a copy of my work document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But it states here, if I'm not mistaken -- at least in the English version, that the date of birth is 7 December 1968. Do you see that on the original -- on the copy in Srpski?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was that your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It was 1963.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who put 1968, in light of the -- sort of the implication that this was a highly efficient administration during the war period in the RS?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who entered this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Next -- that's all for that document. Now, I want to show you -- we're going to go through three documents one by one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And for the record there will be -- the documents I will be handing the gentleman will be P855, P856, and P854. We'll do it in those -- that order. These are all -- these are identification numbers. We're going to go one by one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if you could look at 855, what has been marked as P855. This is a decision, is it not, sir. 855.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not this. It's 856, this one that I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll get it. Do you see this -- this is a decision, is it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a decision assigned to the Sekovici police department as a commander from the 23rd of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- but the decision is dated that it was issued the following day, on the 24th, at the top.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you began working the day before the decision was issued, according to this document.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I worked a lot before. I did that -- those kinds of jobs a lot before, but this is when I actually received the decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Exactly. But what I'm stating is from the decision itself it reflects that at least the date that you started working before the decision was even issued.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was from the Ministry of the Interior. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I want to show you, if you could look at what has been marked for identification purposes as P856. Do you see it, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now this is a decision from the deputy minister, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, deputy minister.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it notes that this decision was issued on 23 August 1995, if you look all the way to the top left-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And again we see that the decision is issued two days after you have -- you were to have taken up your post as a chief of the Zvornik department. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And of course if we went back to the first document, which was P850, the first one that was shown to you by the Prosecutor and that I showed you, here it says August 23, 1995, the date of the decision, but not the date that the decision has in it, which is 21 August 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any explanations why you have these discrepancies?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the slowness of the administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have anything to do with these dates?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, let me show you if you could look at what has been marked for identification purposes as P854. Do you recognise what this document is?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see that it's -- it relates to my years of service or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And does it have anything to do with keeping track of your years of service for social security benefits or retirement benefits?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, yes, it could be that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And here on the first page we see the date 21 August 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you were to go to page 3, it says that -- there we find 23 February 1994, and then further down we find 20 August 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't got that third page -- oh, yes, I have. It's on page 2, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. So at least if we were to look at the previous two documents along with this one, that is Prosecution exhibit for identification 855, 856, and this 854, we at least see that some dates correspond, and that is February 23rd. We see that on all three pages, do we not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 23rd of February is on page 2.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Okay. What I'm suggesting, sir, is that all three documents seem to have the date in various places?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, help me out here. Is it a fact, if you know, that in keeping these records for retirement purposes, every day has to be accounted for?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it ought to be, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me show you another document. This will be the last document. And this is from the Prosecution disclosure material with the ERN number of 01763874. We have an unofficial translation that the Defence did, which is currently being checked and revised officially. This will be marked for identification purposes as D16, the English version, with D16/B as the original version in Srpski. And if we could put this on the ELMO, the English version, if we have an extra copy. This is a decision, is it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is a decision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the decision has a date on it, does it not, on the left corner of March 3rd, 1997?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this decision, this is about your appointment to a position dating to June 1, 1996. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at least in glean -- in looking at this document, it would appear that the decision came out some nine months after you began taking -- you took up your post, assuming that everything is correct. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's like this: Look at what has happened here. They're indicating here that I'm the commander of the detachment from the 22nd of February, 1994, until the 30th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to get to that. Polako, polako.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slowly, slowly, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's deal with one step at a time. If we look at the date when this decision was issued and we look at the other date, it says: 01/06/1996, it would appear that there's a nine-month delay?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this decision is retroactive.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I suppose it would be, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now we'll go to the explanation. Now, the explanation states that on February 24th you took up the duties as the 2nd -- the Sekovici Detachment commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's not what it says --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It says that the decision was dated that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, I'll read it --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And he can ask questions but his interpretation is leading in a cross-examination question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm merely trying to guide the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Read --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- through this maze of paperwork.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Read whatever is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have the date of 24/02/1994. Correct? You see that date under the explanation part?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what is that date -- if you read the explanation, what does that date reflect?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reflects when I received the decision for the first time appointing me as detachment commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, if you look at then the previous date on the decision, 01/06/1996.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. From looking at this decision, what can one conclude?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I was the detachment commander from the 26th of February, 1994, to the 1st of June 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now -- but that, sir, would contradict, would it not, the previous --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- decision. So that we're all clear, in this decision it doesn't reflect what we see in Prosecution's exhibit for identification 856. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you have anything to do with this, by the way?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, I think we got the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if there's going to be an argument on this point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- I would like to make it -- respond to the point, because it clearly does not say what he just said it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll clarify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If he's going to start arguing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll clarify it. I appreciate the assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can we hear the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps he can clear up with further questions, but in looking at this document, the 30 June 1995 is referenced to a regulation that is dated that date, regulation -- it's regulations on the systemisation of posts in the MUP, number K/P-1016 dated 30/06/1995. In another of these documents they refer to the same regulation. In P856 they talk about the same regulation K/P-1016, dated 30 June 1995. So it's hard to say what it means. But there is no reference that this is the ending work date of this man, and -- so that's why -- maybe that can be cleared up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: With pleasure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Mr. McCloskey is absolutely correct. That goes to a decision, that date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, we're going to go step by step. Okay. I want you to look at the last document that I showed you, which is the decision of 3 March 1997. Okay?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, under the part that says "decision," we have a date of 1 June 1996.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what does that date reflect, based on the decision itself?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
