utterances.text: It means that I am deployed to the post of the operations officer for counterintelligence work in the operative centre, Bijeljina, in the centre for intelligence and counterintelligence, as established by the regulations, et cetera, et cetera, and the date is the 1st of June, 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, we can all read, but I just wanted an explanation. Does this mean -- I have to lead a little bit for clarification purposes. Does this mean that June 1 is the starting date of your employment in this new job?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what it should mean, judging from this piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go to the explanation, okay, and it says: "The decision of 096539, and we have it here. It's one of these -- and that would be 85 -- Prosecution Exhibit for identification 855/A, we will see that it has the number on it. And then it says: "Dated 24/02/1994." And it says that you were deployed to the duties and tasks of Sekovici detachment commander. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- so am I correct in interpreting this document to mean that from the -- at least based on its face, that from 24 February 1994 to 1 June 1996, based on this decision, it would appear that you were for that entire period of time the commander of the Sekovici detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by this piece of paper, this decision, yes, that's what it would appear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. But if we then go to Prosecution exhibit for identification 856, which was dated 23 August 1995, a period in between these two dates, it states here that you -- in between these two dates, as of 21 August 1995, you became the chief of the Zvornik department of the anti-terrorist administration. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, just one last thing. This -- because it was raised by the Prosecutor, we have a date of 30 June 1995. Do you see that in the explanation? It says KP --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that date, if I'm not mistaken, refers to a regulation, does it not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's K/P-1016?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, sir. Now, I think that's it for the documents. I just have a couple of minor questions. First of all, the Prosecutor used the word "paperwork," and asked you when you went in on June -- July 15, 1995, whether you did any paperwork. Other than signing these documents, sir, that we know, did you do any paperwork as far as filling out forms, making reports, anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The administration did all that. I just signed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I would suspect that since we have these reports every three months and every six months, there must have been a report that followed this one for the next three-month period starting with July, August, September. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you asked to sign that document, presumably if you had been working into that quarter? Were you ever shown that document to sign it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, when you met with the OTP, with the investigators, you told them about the dates you believed you had been working when you went on vacation, what you did on vacation, and so on and so forth, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they at that time make any requests of you to search for and try to locate any documents that would assist them in determining your whereabouts and your activities and your functions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did ask me about the decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you tell them where they could find the decisions?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I told them, at the MUP.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they ask you to go and try to fetch them, locate them, retrieve them, do that work for them in other words?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had they asked you to go and try to find the paperwork, whether it was still there or in the archives, would you have made any efforts?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you were shown a video at the time that you were questioned by the Prosecution, were you not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, I believe we saw parts of that video here today. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in showing their video, there were times when they would stop the video and ask you some questions and ask you what, if anything or anyone, you recognised in the still -- the frozen frames. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you answer those questions to the best of your ability at the time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, we saw today a photo, a still, of Cop, Trifunovic I believe is his last name. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that frame frozen for you to look at and try to identify the individual, if you recall from reading your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. 2002, when I gave the statement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you by any chance identify the individual and point that out and point out his identity and his association with the 2nd Detachment at the time you were being questioned by the investigators of the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you described a little bit about where the 2nd Detachment was located when you found them on the afternoon or early afternoon hours of 13 July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now -- and again I just want to make sure that I understand and that we all understand. How were they situated?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This has been asked and answered, like he says, yesterday. If there's some specific issue he wants to clear up, I don't have an objection to that. But it looks like we're starting over again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: The question is not clear. "How were they situated," what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying not to draw fire from the other side, Your Honour, on the basis that I'm leading the witness. If I could be given some leeway to give a predicate, which I think is appropriate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Of course. This is re-direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the Prosecution asked you some questions and pointed out some still photos as to what Cop was doing. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, were you with Cop the entire time that you were there visiting your mates?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether all of the troops from the 2nd Detachment were around Cop when that activity was going on?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you seen that activity, the one that we saw on video that is as plain as day, especially after you identified the individual -- but had you seen that, would you have admitted that to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many -- how many tanks and how many Pragas does the 2nd Detachment have?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Detachment had one tank, one Praga, and one three-barrelled BOV.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Well, help me out here, because maybe my math is wrong or maybe I'm too tired and I haven't got the dates right. But there was a document shown to you by the Prosecution, and I believe it's 853 for identification purposes. If we could show you this document, maybe you can help us out here a little bit. Do you have that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want you to go to the section that says: "State of readiness in the unit headquarters." That would be page 7. If we could put that on the ELMO, please. And it would be page 4 for you, sir, in Srpski. All right.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to count the lines. It says one, two, three, the third line where it says: "Between 18 March 1995 and 30 June 1995, a tank crew was in the state of readiness in Bratunac." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And now if you go all the way down to the end, the very last one, it says: "Between 1 May 1995 and 30 June 1995, a tank crew was in a state of readiness in the unit headquarters," and I believe that would be Sekovici. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, it would seem that these dates overlap, do they not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if there's only one tank for the unit, how can the tank be in two different places at the same time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably somebody made a mistake who compiled this report, the administration, I assume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you compile this report?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, that was done by the administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okey-doke. Now, if we go down to line 5, here we do have the one -- we have a Praga, right, between 1 March 1995 and 31st March 1995. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What line did you say?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I said line 5 where it says: "Between 1st March 1995 and 31st March 1995, a Praga" --

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And then if we go to the next line, there you see 1 April 1995 and 30 April 1995. There we have a tank crew and a Praga.

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. With the tank, I guess we see some discrepancies again. Right?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Probably they made an error when they compiled this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So now we have it in three different places, but with the Praga it would appear that that could have occurred, March 1 to 31st March, and then 1 April. So the dates at least correspond. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we stay with this report and we go to the end of the page, the last part, this was pointed out and the Prosecution highlighted the word "cooperation," though in his questioning he was using the word "coordination," but I would suspect that is the same, cooperation, coordination, in the context in which the question was posed on cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you would -- would cooperation also mean resubordination?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It could mean that, but not necessarily. People can cooperate whether they are in a subordinate-superior relation or whether they are equals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything in here, though, that says that when the Sekovici detachment unit was in any of these locations, that they were subordinated and were working under and being controlled by and ordered by VRS units?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In reading this document, 853, where it talks about cooperation, does it say anything about resubordination?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is there anything in that document, incidentally, about cooperation with the Bratunac Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS STUPAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you very much, Mr. Stupar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any re-direct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We certainly would -- D115, D116 -- okay. D115 is the conversation between Kazimierz Piekos and Milos Stupar conducted on June 2002. This is the transcript of his statement given to the OTP. D116 is the decision that we introduced just now on redirect of 3 March 1997. And in light of the fact that we made reference to the other documents that were given to us by the Prosecution and that are listed on their exhibit list, we would propose that P850, P851, P854, P855, and P856 also come in. And if we need to give them D numbers, we are happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, there's no foundation for any of these documents, Your Honour, but it's all the Prosecution's documents. So Mr. Karnavas will withdraw his foundation requests or his objection to the last group of documents I offered into the same thing, we might be able to reach what is more reasonable. I have no objection truly to any of these documents coming in. And I would suggest that I can add the declaration that we've done for the other documents, we'll add these documents in as well so that the Court can see where all this stuff came from. And I don't have any objections. The interview statement of this witness, you know, I have no objection to the Court viewing it either, because it's -- from what I gather, the only subject or reason for it is the attack on the integrity of the Prosecutor, which I don't think it should be -- that there's any substance to that attack. But if it's made, I have no objection to you reviewing that statement, as you can clearly see that there's no problem in that statement. So I don't have any objection to any of this material, and we should just add to it 850 and 853, which are the documents that I think I mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections to document P853 by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: By the Prosecution? I have no objection to all of these documents. I just wanted to note that I have the official translation of P -- D116. We've just -- were able to get it. And as far as the comments, it was not meant to be an attack on the Prosecution. What I was trying to demonstrate is that in spite of the cautionary language used by the Prosecutor, the gentleman gave a statement, answered all the questions, and I think that is something that needs to be considered in factoring in the gentleman's credibility. I think that was the purpose of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, as this witness would probably readily admit, many times in an interview or interrogation, you tell the person what you think of what they're saying. It was done forthrightly and honestly. I remember him well. We had a long chat. It ended with his having no complaints. So the implication that there was something wrong here that we had to live through the other day is -- in any event, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as a principle that the previous statement will not be admitted into the evidence. But since the Defence counsel insisted that this piece of the documents goes to the credibility of this witness and there is no strong objections from the Prosecution, so the document D115 is admitted into the evidence as well as D116, P850, P851, P853, P854, P855, and P856. After this sitting, the Defence may consult with the Court Deputy for the Defence numbers on the same documents. It is so decided. Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence; we appreciate it very much. The usher will show you out of the room. Please feel free to go now. We wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that we exhausted the witness list for this week, but I have to remind Defence counsel that all together we are one day behind the original schedule. And also, we don't think this witness helped us a lot, because we are only interested in the subordination or resubordination issues from the testimony of this witness. I don't think there is any differences between the parties that terrible things happened in certain times, in certain areas. But the most important thing for this case is the linkage of your clients and that incident. This is what we want to hear from the future witnesses. So I hope -- and we see there's still room for improvement of the direct examination, as well as for the cross-examination, of course. And we have to make the best use for the time availability to us. The deadline is there, and we have to do our utmost to make it. Well, this is what I want to say at this stage. Are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise at this stage? Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. We are working on our -- the work we've mentioned before on the joint motion. And no problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
